result.topic_en: Two facing pages (302–303). On 302 Euler ends the treatment of divisors of pp+30qq: their four classes, a conjecture that all residual numbers 120i+a are divisors, and the list of primes up to 240. On 303 he begins Example 11, the prime divisors of pp−30qq.
result.transcription:
[p. 302]
I. $D=F$; II. $2D=F$; III. $3D=F$; IV. $5D=F$;
vbi notasse iuuabit, si fuerit $2D=F$, tum etiam fore $15D=F$; similique modo si fuerit $3D=F$, erit etiam $10D=F$; at si fuerit $5D=F$, erit etiam $6D=F$.

Corollarium 2.
§. 34. Quando dicimus, omnes diuisores numerorum formae propositae $pp+30qq$ in forma $120i+a$ contineri, id non ita est intelligendum, quasi omnes numeri in formula $120i+a$ contenti essent diuisores, sed inde excludi debent omnes illi, qui per quempiam numerum formae $120i+\alpha$ sunt diuisibiles. His autem sublatis maxime probabile videtur, omnes reliquos numeros formulae $120i+a$, ideoque imprimis numeros primos, certe fore diuisores cuiuspiam numeri formae $pp+30qq$. Isti autem numeri primi in formula $120i+a$ contenti facili negotio quousque libuerit assignari possunt, quippe qui hoc ordine vsque ad 240 progrediuntur
1, 11, 13, 17, 23, 29, 31, 37, 43, 47, 59, 67, 79, 101, 113, 131, 137, 149, 151, 157, 163, 167, 179, 199, 233.

Corollarium 3.
§. 35. Quoniam omnes diuisores sunt quadruplicis generis, inde etiam valores ipsius $a$ in quatuor classes distribui conueniet, prouti inde oriuntur diuisores vel primae, vel secundae, vel tertiae, vel quartae classis, quibus ergo subscribamus characteres cuiusque classis 1, 2, 3, 6, hoc modo:
1, 11, 13, 17, 23, 29, 31, 37, 43, 47, 49, 59, 67, 79, 101, 113
1, 6, 3, 2, 2, 6, 1, 3, 3, 2, 1, 6, 3, 1, 6, 2.
Hic igitur notari meretur, singulas classes quater occurrere.
Exem-

[p. 303]
Exemplum 11.
§. 36. Inuenire omnes diuisores primos numerorum in hac forma: $pp-30qq$, siue in hac: $30pp-qq$ contentorum.

Solutio.
Cum hic sit $\sqrt{\frac{30}{5}}$ [?] $<3$, pro littera $g$ habemus tantum tres valores 0, 1, 2. Hinc cum sit $fh=30-gg$, pro primo casu erit $fh=30$, pro secundo $fh=29$ et pro tertio $fh=26$, quos igitur casus euoluamus.
I. Sit $g=0$ et hinc nascuntur sequentes valores:
1°. $D=rr-30ss$,
2°. $D=2rr-15ss$,
3°. $D=3rr-10ss$,
4°. $D=5rr-6ss$.
II. Si $g=1$ vnica forma nascitur
$D=rr+2rs-29ss=(r+s)^2-30ss$,
quae ergo est ipsa forma proposita.
III. Si $g=2$ oriuntur duae formulae
1°. $D=rr+4rs-26ss=(r+2s)^2-30ss$:
iterum ipsa proposita;
2°. $D=2rr+4rs-13ss$,
cuius duplum fit numerus formae propositae. Hinc ergo nascuntur quadruplicis generis diuisores, qui posita littera $F$ pro formula proposita sunt
I. $D=F$. II. $2D=F$. III. $3D=F$. IV. $6D=F$.
Deinde vero pro formula omnes diuisores continente $120i+a$ erit primo vel $a=pp$, vel $a=\frac{pp}{2}$ [?] vel $a=\frac{pp}{3}$ [?] vel $a=\frac{pp}{6}$ [?],
vnde

items.quote: His autem sublatis maxime probabile videtur, omnes reliquos numeros formulae $120i+a$, ideoque imprimis numeros primos, certe fore diuisores cuiuspiam numeri formae $pp+30qq$.
items.english: But once these are removed, it seems most probable that all the remaining numbers of the formula 120i+a, and therefore especially the prime numbers, will certainly be divisors of some number of the form pp+30qq.

items.quote: Hic igitur notari meretur, singulas classes quater occurrere.
items.english: Here it therefore deserves to be noted that each of the classes occurs four times.

items.quote: Inuenire omnes diuisores primos numerorum in hac forma: $pp-30qq$, siue in hac: $30pp-qq$ contentorum.
items.english: To find all prime divisors of numbers contained in the form pp−30qq, or in the form 30pp−qq.
